An N-terminal fragment of chromogranin A, residues 1-76, with a disulfide bond between C17 and C38.

Activity against filamentous fungi (MIC 5-30 uM): N. crassa, A. fumigatus, A. brassicola, N. haematococca, F. culmorum, F. oxyporum, and T. mentagrophytes (Lugardon K et al., 2001). Original AP1478 for Chromofungin has been merged here.

SAR: Synthetic derivatives studies revealed chromogranin A-(47-66), called Chromofungin, is the most active shortest form.

Structure: 3D Structure of Chromofungin, determined in 50% TFE, is helical.

MOA: Chromofungin appears to act on cell wall and memrbanes. It may also inhibit intracellular calmodulin-dependent enzymes. Updated 5/2016; 7/2021.

02354.Name_Class: mBD-3 (murine beta defensin-3, UCSS1a; natural AMPs; animals; 3S=S)
02354.Additional_info:
Murine homolog of HBD-2.

Recombinant production:insects:Spodoptera frugiperda (Sf9): Recombinant mBD-3 peptide, produced from a baculovirus cell expression system, showed antimicrobial activity against P. aeruginosa PAO1 (MIC 8 um/ml) and E. coli D31 (MIC 16 ug/ml) in a salt-sensitive manner (see the ref).

Discovery: Host expression:induced: pathogen inducible. mBD-3 appears to play a role in mucosal immunity in the lower urinary tract(Becknell B et al. 2014 IL-17A and IL-17F are essential for the production of mBD-3 to clear S. aureus nasal colonization (Archer NK et al., 2016).

Activity: synthetic mBD-3 inhibited the growth of E. coli, P. aeruginosa, S. aureus, and C. albicans at concentrations from 25 to 50 microg/mL (Burd RS et al 2002).

Updated 4/2014; 10/2016; 3/2017; Jan2024.

02355.Name_Class: Mastoparan-X (MPX, peptide 12a; natural AMPs; insects, arthropods, invertebrates, animals; XXA)

It also stimulates phospholipase A2 activity and activates G proteins.

In vitro toxicity: human RBC: HC50 349.4 uM; rat RBC: HC50 156.5 uM. Less hemo.lytic (Ye et al., 2023).

Structure: The C-terminal 12 residues adopted helical conformation upon binding to membranes (Wakamatsu K et al., 1992).

Discoveryy: Found in multiple species.

02368.Additional_info:
Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals this sequence is most similar (83.33%) to

Mol formula: C66H109N21O18; Mol Wt: 1484.725; Mol Ex Coeff: 0; GRAVY: -0.14.

Activity: Active against C. albicans 01U or 38 U (MIC 10 ug/ml), C. parapsilosis (MIC 32 ug/ml), C. neoformans L26 (MIC 64 ug/ml), C. neoformans L30 (MIC 64 ug/ml), T.mentagrophytes (MIC 128 ug/ml), and T. rubrum (MIC 10 ug/ml).

In vitro toxicity: MTT assay: mouse macrophage line RAW 264.7, Cm-p5 showed no toxicity at 400 ug/ml; human RBC: not hemo.lytic at 400 ug/ml.

Structure: the peptide is helical based on both CD and NMR. You can rotate, zoom, and view the crystal structure 2BZZ here in the PDB.

MOA: biophysical studies using liposomes suggest a membrane surface covering without memrbane permeation (Gonzalez-Garcia et al., 2024).

SAR: Compared to the WT, Cm-p5 (Cm-p1 appended with LF at the C-terminus) has increased antifungal actvity but low toxicity to mammalian cells. Cm-p3 (appended with RC at the C-terminus) and Cm-p4 (appended with MK at the C-terminus) are more or less similar to Cm-P1 with moderate or weak antifungal activity. These results suggest the need of a hydrophobic pair for improved activity.

Animal model:mouse failed: In a systemic candidiasis model in mice, intraperitoneal administration of Cm-p5 at 5 or 25 mg/kg was unable to control the fungal kidney burden. In contrast, amphotericin B was able to.

The original entry VCP-VT1 (insect peptide) shares the seqquence with Temporin-1CSb (frog peptide) and therefore it has been merged with AP595. 2/2023; 11/2024.

02374.Name_Class: Frenatin 2.1S (natural AMPs; frogs, amphibians, animals; XXA; UCLL1c)
02374.Additional_info:
Activity: Active against reference strains S. aureus and S. epidermidis (MIC 8-16 uM), E. faecalis, C. albicans (MIC 62.5 uM), A. baumannii clinical isolates NM8, NM35, and NM75 (MIC 62.5 uM), S. maltophilia clinical isolates (B32/1 B32/4 U8908 B5/5 B6/2) (MIC 31-62 uM). Active against plant pathogens X. axonopodis pv. vesicatoria (MIC 3.1-6.2 uM) (Camó C et al. 2018). Showed a poor hemolysis of human erythrocytes (LC50 >160 uM).

Also active against non-small cell lung adenocarcinoma A549 cells (LC50 80 uM).

It is propsoed that this peptide has proinflammatory action and promotes cytotoxic capability of NK cells on 4T1 mouse mammary carcinoma cells (Pantic et al., 2017).

Updated 5/2017.

02376.Name_Class: Lassomycin (natural AMPs; Gram-positive bacteria, prokaryotes; lasso, XXJ; lactam; UCSB1a)
02376.Additional_info:
Chemical modification: It resembles lassos since the carboxylic side chain of Asp8 forms a bond with the N-terminal Gly.

Activity: Active against both growing and dormant mycobacteria, including drug-resistant M. tuberculosis (anti-TB).

MOA:bacteria:lassomycin binds to a highly acidic region of the ClpC1 ATPase complex. ClpC1 ATPase is an essential enzyme in mycobacteria. This mechanism, uncoupling ATPase from proteolytic activity, accounts for the bactericidal activity of lassomycin.

Structure: NMR structure of the cyclic peptide has been solved. You can rotate, zoom, and view the 3D structure here in the PDB. in addition, high-resolution crystal structure of the N-terminal domain of ClpC1 (ClpC1 NTD) in complex with Lassomycin provides insight into the binding mode (Jagdev et al., 2023). the complex structure is here in the PDB. The peptide forms a beta-sheet structure in the crystal.

Updated 10/2023; structure 7/2025

02377.Name_Class: Tk-AMP-X2 (natural AMPs; alpha-hairpinin structural family; plants)
02377.Additional_info: Activity: Active against F. graminearum (IC50 7.5 ug/ml), F. verticillioides (10 ug/ml), D. maydis (17 ug/ml). You can rotate, zoom, and view the 3D structure here in the PDB. Updated 5/2015.

02375.Name_Class: Frenatin 2.2S (natural AMPs; frogs, amphibians, animals; XXA; UCLL1c; others: Frenatin 2.3S
02375.Additional_info:
Activity: Active against reference strains S. aureus and S. epidermidis (MIC 8-16 uM), E. faecalis, C. albicans (MIC 62.5 uM), A. baumannii clinical isolates NM75 (MIC 62.5 uM), S. maltophilia clinical isolates B32/1 B32/4 U8908 B5/5 B6/2 (MIC 31-62 uM). Active against plant pathogens X. axonopodis pv. vesicatoria and X. arboricola pv. pruni (MIC 6.2-12.5 uM) (Camó C et al. 2018).

Also active against non-small cell lung adenocarcinoma A549 cells (LC50 65 uM).

In vitro toxicity: Showed a poor hemolysis of human erythrocytes (HC50 >160 uM): hemo.lytic. Cf: Frenatin 2.3S (GLVGTLLGHIGKAILG, no C-terminal amidation) showed only weak antimicrobial activity (>100 uM).

12/2018; 4/2025 GW.

02378.Name_Class: Gageostatin A (natural AMPs; Leu-rich; UCLL1c; nonribosomal peptide; lipopeptides; marine bacteria, prokaryotes; XXD; XXL; other forms: Gageostatin B; Gageostatin C)
02378.Additional_info:
Gageostatins possess the same amino acid sequence but different lipid anchor at the N-terminus. Gageostatin A has a C14 fatty acid chain; Gageostatin B: lipid: 3-beta-hydroxy-9,11-dimethyltridecanoic acid, C15 fatty acid; Gageostatin C: lipid: (E)-7,9-dimethylundec-2-enoic acid, C13 fatty acid chain.

Activity: Active against pathogenic fungi R. solani, B. cinerea and C. acutatum (MIC 4-32 ug/mL); moderately active against bacteria B. subtilis, S. aeureus, S. typhi and P. aeruginosa (MICs 8-64 ug/mL). In addition, Gageostatins 1-3 displayed cytotoxicity against six human cancer cell lines with 50% inhibition value EC50 values of 4.6-19.6 ug/mL. Updated 5/2016; 10/2021

02379.Additional_info:
Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals this sequence is most similar (53.33%) to

L:47%; R:20%; K=Q: 13%. Mol formula: C87H162N28O18; Mol Wt: 1888.418; Mol Ex Coeff: 0; GRAVY: -0.22.

Activity: active against Gram+ B. subtilis (MIC 2 ug/ml), E. faecalis (MIC 2 ug/ml), E. faecium VRE (MIC 2 ug/ml) (anti-VRE. cf.: MIC of vancomycin >32 ug/ml), M. luteus (MIC 2 ug/ml), S. aureus or MRSA (MIC 2 ug/ml), Gram- E. coli (MIC 2 ug/ml), P. aeruginosa (MIC 2 ug/ml), S. typhimurium (MIC 2 ug/ml), fungi C. albicans (MIC 2 ug/ml), C. neoformans (MIC 2 ug/ml), and S. cerevisiae (MIC 2 ug/ml).

Antimicrobial robustness: salt-insensitive; MIC increased 2-4 fold in the presence of 150 mM NaCl (2 fold Gram+ and 4-fold Gram- and fungi); serum-sensitive: MIC increased 2-16 fold with 10% serum (2-4 Gram+, 16 fold Gram-, and 4-8 fold fungi). Protease stability: resistant to digestion by trypsin and aureolysin, but slightly cleaved by chymotrypsin after 12 h incubation.

Toxicity: not hemo.lytic till 130 ug/ml. cell viability not reduced after 24 h treatment of HaCaT keratinocytes and BJ fibroblasts till 70 ug/ml.

Structure: helical in 20 mM SDS.

MOA: Caused damage to membranes via permeabilization.

02380.Name_Class: salivaricin A2 (lantibiotic, XXT3; class 1 bacteriocin, natural AMPs; UCLSS1; Gram-positive bacteria, prokaryotes; BBW)
02380.Additional_info:
Chemical modification:three thionine rings: T9-C14, T11-C21, and S17-C22.

Activity: Active against M. luteus ATCC 10240 (MIC 2 ug/ml), C. accolens ATCC 49725 (MIC 8 ug/ml), C. accolens KPL 1818 (MIC 16 ug/ml), C. accolens KPL 2060 (MIC 8 ug/ml), C. accolens KPL 2061 (MIC 16 ug/ml), C. pseudodiphtheriticum KPL 1989 (MIC 8 ug/ml), C. striatum KPL 1959 (MIC 32 ug/ml), C. accolens KPL 1855 (MIC 16 ug/ml), S. pneumoniae ATCC 27336 (MIC 32 ug/ml), (MIC 2 ug/ml), S. pneumoniae AI8 (MIC 32 ug/ml), S. pneumoniae AI11 (MIC 16 ug/ml), S. pneumoniae AI14 (MIC 16 ug/ml), S.pneumoniae AI6 (MIC 128 ug/ml), S.pneumoniae AI7 (MIC 128 ug/ml), S.mutans JH1140 (MIC >128 ug/ml), (MIC 16 ug/ml), S. salivarius HS0302 (MIC 64 ug/ml), B.subtilis PY79 (MIC >128 ug/ml), B.megaterium ATCC 14581 (MIC >128 ug/ml), S.epidermidis ERIN 30713 (MIC >128 ug/ml), S.aureus ATCC 25923 (MIC >128 ug/ml), and E.faecalis ERIN 30002 (MIC >128 ug/ml) (Geng et al., 2018).

MOA:bacteria: binds to lipid II with low affinity.

The original has been merged into AP2378 due to the same sequence 3/2023

02381.Name_Class: Gageotetrin A (natural AMPs; nonribosomal peptide; lipopeptides;  marine bacteria, prokaryote; XXL)
02381.Additional_info:
Chemical modification: The N-terminal C14 fatty acid is a 3-hydroxy-11-methyltridecanoic acid (HTDA).

Activity: It is more active against fungi compared to bacteria with MIC values of 0.02-0.04 uM. Inhibited S. aureus (MIC 0.03 uM), B. subtilis (MIC 0.03 uM), S. typhi (MIC 0.06 uM), P. aeruginosa (MIC 0.06 uM), R. solani (MIC 0.06 uM), C. acutatum (MIC 0.03 uM), B. cinera (MIC 0.03 uM).

Toxicity: not toxic to numerous human cancer cells at 30 ug/ml. Corrected 5/2016; 7/2021.

02384.Name_Class: Raniseptin 1 (Rsp-1, natural AMPs; frogs, amphibians, animals; UCLL1; More AMPs? Rsp-2, Rsp-3, Rsp-4, Rsp-5, Rsp-6, Rsp-7, Rsp-8, Rsp-9)
02384.Additional_info:
Activity: Active against E. coli (MIC 5 uM), P. aeruginosa (MIC 10 uM), and S. aureus (MIC 20 uM).

Antimicrobial activities for other peptides in the family, including Rsp-2, Rsp-3, Rsp-4, Rsp-5, Rsp-6, Rsp-7, Rsp-8, and Rsp-9, are not yet available. Updated 7/2021

02382.Name_Class: Gageotetrin B  (natural AMPs; Leu-rich; UCLL1c; nonribosomal peptide; lipopeptides; marine bacteria, prokaryote; XXL; Variant: Gageotetrin C)
02382.Additional_info:
Chemical modification: E is a methoxy-Glu (esterized). The N-terminal C14 fatty acid is a 3-hydroxy-11-methyltridecanoic acid (HTDA).

Variant: In the case of Gageotetrin C, the N-terminal C14 fatty acid is a 3-hydroxy-8,10-dimethyldodecanoic acid (HDDA).

Activity: They are more active against fungi compared to bacteria. Inhibited S. aureus (MIC 0.04 uM), B. subtilis (MIC 0.02-0.04 uM), S. typhi (MIC 0.02 uM), P. aeruginosa (MIC 0.02-0.04 uM), R. solani (MIC 0.02 uM), C. acutatum (MIC 0.01-0.02 uM), B. cinera (MIC 0.01 uM). In addiiton, gageotetrins B and C displayed good time course motility inhibition and lytic activity against the late blight pathogen P. capsici, which causes enormous economic damage in cucumber, pepper, tomato and beans, at 0.02 uM.

Toxicity: not toxic to numerous human cancer cells at 30 ug/ml. Updated 5/2016; 7/2021.

02385.Name_Class: P1-Hp-1971 (natural AMPs; frogs, amphibians, animals; XXA; UCLL1c. More AMPs?)
02385.Additional_info: These H. pulchellus (Hp) peptides (AP2385 to AP2387) were named based on peptide identification number. There are 23% glycines and 19% prolines in the sequence.  Active against S. aureus (MIC 8 uM) and E. coli (MIC 13 uM). There are more peptides reported in this peptidomic study. Their activity data are not available.

02383.Name_Class: Arenicin-1 V8R analog (synthetic AMPs20; Arg-rich; UCSS1a; 1S=S; variants: many more analogs)
02383.Additional_info:
Sequence analysis: This single residue analog is 95.24% similar to its parent molecule (AP00727). R: 33%; V: 19%; Y: 14%; C=W: 10%. GRAVY: -0.48; M.Wt: 2817.398; mol formula: C128H200N44O25S2.

Activity: Active against S. aureus strain 209P (MIC 6.25 uM), E. coli strain C600 (1.56 uM), and P. aeruginosa PAO1 (MIC 1.56 uM).

Structure: similar to the WT. You can rotate, zoom, and view the 3D structure here in the PDB.

Toxicity: This peptide became much less hemo.lytic (sellectivity improved by 50 fold with similar activity) than its parent peptide due to reduced hydrophobicity. 10% hemolysis at 125 uM (cf. 4.1 uM for the WT). Not hemo.lytic.

The original has been merged with AP2382. Updated 7/2021; 2/2023.

02386.Name_Class: P2-Hp-1935 (Hp-1935; natural AMPs; frogs, amphibians, animals; XXA; UCLL1c)
02386.Additional_info: The sequence contains 21% leucines, 15% glycines, serines, and lysines. Active against S. aureus (MIC 66 uM) and E. coli (MIC 33 uM). Helical in TFE and liposomes. Also, this peptide can inhibit acetylcholinesterase (AChE), an enzyme involved in non-cholinergic processes as the stimulation of the amyloid-beta peptide aggregation and neurotoxicity (Sanchis et al., 2020). Updated Jan2020

02388.Name_Class: BPTI (Bovine Pancreatic Trypsin Inhibitor; UCSS1a; natural AMPs; cattle, ruminant, mammals, animals; 3S=S)
02388.Additional_info: Originally found as an enzyme inhibitor in the 1930s. Cys residues exist at conserved positions 5, 14, 30, 38, 51 and 55. High stability of BPTI towards temperature, acids, bases, organic 55 solvents and proteolytic degradation has been reported (Fritz et al., 1983). It served as a model small protein for NMR studies in many aspects. There are over NMR+X-ray 100 structures for WT, mutants, and complexed forms of BPTI in the PDB. You can rotate, zoom, and view the crystal structure of BPTI in complex with trypsin here in the PDB. In 2014, it was established as an antifungal AMP with a novel mechanism of action (MOA) by inhibiting Mg2+ uptake. Consistent with this 152 notion, overexpression of ALR1 rescued the BPTI-dependent growth inhibition. Active against C. albicans (IC50 10 uM) and S. cerevisiae (IC50 4.5 uM).

02393.Name_Class: P-10 (Lys-rich; UCLL1, natural AMPs; tunicate, marine invertebrates, animals)
02393.Additional_info: Predicted from genome followed by experiment validation.  Active against E. coli, P. vulgaris,  Gram-positive S. aureus, S. mutans, and M. tetragenus based on inhibition zone assays.

02284.Name_Class: CPF-St5 (natural AMPs; frog, amphibians, animals; UCLL1)
02284.Additional_info:
Activity: Active against Gram- E. coli (MIC 1 uM), P. aeruginosa (MIC 4-8 uM), Gram+ S. aureus (MIC 1 uM), M. luteus (MIC 0.5 uM), yeast S. cerevisiae (MIC 16 uM), and parasite T. brucei (LC95 1-2 uM).

Toxicity: Toxicity to erythrocytes (HC50 64 uM) moderate hemolytic and T-lymphocytes (IC50 8 uM). Updated 7/2021

Active against Gram+ M. luteus LB 14110, S. aureus ATCC 6538, L. ivanovii BUG 496, E. faecalis JH 2-2, Gram- bacteria E. coli ATCC 8739, S. typhimurium, S. enterica ATCC 43972, A. tumefaciens, P. savastanoi pv. savastanoi, P. aeruginosa ATCC 49189,  fungistatic against C. tropicalis R2 CIP203 and Fusarium. sp. based on inhibition zone 13-33 mm).  Updated 3/2020

02396.Name_Class: Amylocyclicin  (natural AMPs; bacteriocins, Gram-positive bacteria, prokaryotes; XXC; UCBB1aA)

02397.Name_Class: Sonorensin  (Cys-rich; natural AMPs; bacteriocins, Gram-positive bacteria, prokaryotes)
02397.Additional_info: Both L. monocytogenes (MIC 1 ug/ml) and V. vulnificus (MIC 25 ug/ml) are highly sensitive. Also active against  B. subtilis (MIC 50 ug/ml), S. aureus (MIC 45 ug/ml), P. aeruginosa (MIC 43 ug/ml), and E. coli (MIC 96 ug/ml). Updated 10/2020

02394.Name_Class: Thurincin H  (natural AMPs; sactipeptide; bacteriocins, Gram-positive bacteria, prokaryotes; 4S=CA; XXJ; UCSB1c)
02394.Additional_info:
Activity: diffusion assays: active against B. cereus F4552, B. thuringiensis EG10368, and L. monocytogenes 2289. In a separate study, also active against B. cereus 183 (MIC 5 ug/ml), E. faecium wild type (11,197 U), and E. faecium ATCC 19,434 (6950 U) (Ortiz-Rodríguez T, et al., 2022).

SAR: alanine scan reveals that W2A, C4A, W5A, C7A, L8A, C10A, C13A, L17A, N19A, T22A, and T29A lost activity.

Structure: There are four unique S-Calpha thioether bonds that crosslink the two helices (Sit CS et al., 2011). You can rotate, zoom, and view the crystal structure of BPTI in complex with trypsin here in the PDB.

Toxicity: no hemolysis at 20 ug/ml (4xMIC). Updated 7/2021

02398.Name_Class: Perfrin (natural AMPs; antimicrobial protein; bacteriocins, Gram-positive bacteria, prokaryotes)
02398.Additional_info: Inhibited multiple Broiler C. perfringens strains. This bacteriocin did not show clear homology with currently known bacteriocins, indicating a new member. Updated 10/2020

02399.Name_Class: Sil (natural AMPs; bacteriocins, Gram-positive bacteria, prokaryotes)
02399.Additional_info: SIL is secreted by S. iniae into the extracellular milieu. Although it displayed antibacterial activity against B. subtilis, SIL showed no effect on 22 other Gram+ and Gram- bacteria tested. It can attach to the B. subtilis surface without killing (bacteriostatic). Activity is lost by heating at 50oC (heat-sensitive). SIL may serve as a virulent factor for infection. This dual role as antimicrobial and immune modulator suggests that a good understanding of the functions of an AMP is essential.  Updated 8/2014.

02400.Name_Class: CFBD-1  (C. fudingensis beta defensin-1; defensins; 3S=S,  UCSS1a; natural AMPs; salamanders, amphibians, animals)
02400.Additional_info: 38% similar to cod beta defensin (AP2219). Active against S. aureus ATCC 25923 (MIC 65 ug/ml) and weakly active against B. subtilis ATCC 6633, E.coli ATCC 25922, and C.albicans (MIC 135-200 ug/ml). Updated 6/2020

02402.Name_Class: Garvicin A (GarA; natural AMPs; class 2d bacteriocin, Gram-positive bacteria, prokaryotes; BBrcp)
02402.Additional_info: ~33% similar to AP840: insect Gm-mlpD. Bactericidal against the trout pathogen L. garvieae 8831. The extracellular loop of Man-PTS subunit IID is responsible for the sensitivity of Lactococcus garvieae to garvicins A, B and C (Tymoszewska et al. 2018). Updated 5/2019

02405.Additional_info: APD analysis reveals 76.9% sequence similarity to AP1178: bacteriocin Plantaricin JK. Active against S. aureus (MIC 35.2 ug/ml), K. pneumoniae, P. aeruginosa, P. lilacinum, and A. niger (MIC 62-72 ug/ml). Showed 1% hemolysis at 100 ug/ml.

02401.Name_Class: BTM-P1 (synthetic AMPs20; Ala-rich; ZZI; BBMm, UCLL1)
02401.Additional_info: ~42% similar to AP1959: frog Temporin-HN1. Artificially synthesized based on the bacterial Cry11Bb protein, which is toxic to mosquito larvae. The sequence has been patented. At 7.1 uM, this synthetic peptide inhibited the growth of E. coli ATCC 25922, S. aureus ATCC 25923, S. pneumoniae ATCC 49619, H. influenzae ATCC 49247, E. faecalis ATCC 29212, P. aeruginosa ATCC27603, P. aeruginosa (Multi-Resistant), and K. pneumoniae ATCC70603 (Segura C et al., 2007). In addition, the protease-resistant BTM-P1d (i.e., synthesized using D-amino acids), not the BTM-P1 synthesized in L-amino acids, displayed A. aegypti larval toxicity (Lemeshko VV, Orduz S., 2013). It adopts a helical conformation in 30% TFE. MOA: it appears to permeate membranes. Deposited and provided by Sergio Orduz on May 6, 2014. APD release May 8, 2014.

02403.Name_Class: Hp1404 (natural AMPs; scorpions, arachnids, Chelicerata, arthropods, invertebrates, animals; UCLL1a; Derivatives: K1K8)
02403.Additional_info:
Sequence analysis: ~82% similar to AP2334: scorpion Hp1036.

Activity: Active against only tested Gram-positive bacteria, including S. aureus AB94004 (also others strains ATCC25923, ATCC6538, AB208193), S. epidermidis AB208187 (also AB208188), M. luteus AB93113, B. subtilis AB91021, S. aureus MRSA P1381, S. aureus MRSA P1374, E. faecium, and S. agalactiae (MIC 4-16 uM).

In vitro toxicity: human RBC: HC50 226 ug/ml, less hemo.lytic (10% hemolysis at 100 ug/ml). Cytoxicity: 10-30% at 100 ug/ml to HFF, 293T and A375 cells.

In vivo toxicity:mouse:IP: 80 mg/kg mice survived after 7 days. In vivo toxicity:mouse:IV: 5-10 mg/kg ok; 66.6% survived at 80 mg/kg and no survival at 160 mg/kg.

Animal model:mouse:survival:peritonitis model, the injected peptide did protect the mice in vivo compared to the untreated group.

Antimicrobial robustness: Serum, but not salt, might have reduced peptide activity in vivo (Salt-insensitive but serum-sensitive).

Structure: Helical in TFE.

SAR: Changes residues 1 and 8 to lysines (K1K8) led to increased activity and reduced hemolysis.

Resistance development:no:bacteria:S. aureus AB94004: after 15 passages, but kanamycin and ampicillin did (Li et al., 2016).

Updated 5/2016; 4/2024; 6/2025.

02404.Name_Class: Taromycin A (natural AMPs; lipopeptides; lactone; depsipeptide, nonribosomal peptide;  marine bacteria, prokaryote; XXH; XXD3; XXL; XXJ; UCSB1b)
02404.Additional_info: ~82% similar to AP2203: daptomycin. The authors used a transformation-associated recombination (TAR)-based genetic platform to directly clone, refactor, and heterologously express a silent biosynthetic pathway to yield a new antibiotic analog of daptomycin. The marine actinomycete Saccharomonospora sp. CNQ-490 TAR gene cluster was successfully expressed. Taromycin A differs from Daptomycin only in serveal places: 1) residue T11 is an D-Ala; 2) W is chlorinated at position 6; 3) Kny is also chlorinated at position 4; and 4) it carried an octa-2,4-dienoyl lipid side chain. Warning: the sequence is a close mimic of the natural counterpart. For example, kynurenine-13 (Kyn) is represented by Y here. Refer to daptomycin for more details. Active against MRSA 0325 (MIC 12 ug/ml), E. faecalis 613, E. faecalis 447 (MIC 6 ug/ml), E. faecalis 613D, E. faecium 447D (MIC 50 ug/ml), and VRE 5938 (100 ug/ml) (anti-VRE). It is a potential lead. UPdated 9/2017.

02406.Name_Class: Mytichitin-A (mytichitin-1, UCSS1a; natural AMPs; mollusca/molluscs/mollusks, marine invertebrates, animals; 3S=S)
02406.Additional_info:
Sequence analysis: ~30% similar to AP342: plant Mc-AMP1. Warning: position 39 is X in the original amino acid sequence. It is represented in A in this database.

Activity: Active against Gram-negative bacteria E. coli (MIC 25-50 uM), V. harveyi (MIC 25-50 uM), V-parahaemolyticus (MIC>50 uM), P-aeruginosa (MIC > 50 uM), Gram-positive B. subtilis (MIC 1.2-1.5 uM), S. aureus (MIC 2.5-5.0 uM), S. luteus (MIC 1.2-1.5 uM), B. megaterium (2.5-5 uM), and fungi C. albicans (MIC 6.7-12.5 uM).

Recombinant production:plants:Chlamydomonas reinhardti: Transgenic plants: tantem repeat of this peptide (3X) was expressed and reached 0.28% of total soluble protein.

In vitro toxicity: the recombinant form was active but did not show toxicity to HEK293 cells (Dong et al., 2018).

Updated 12/2024

02407.Additional_info: Active against E. coli, P. aeruginosa, B. cereus, S. enterica and S. aureus based on disc diffusion assays. This peptide is also antioxidant since at 40 ug/mL Hispidalin exhibited 70.8% DPPH free radical-scavenging activity and 69.5% lipid peroxide inhibition. Reg5/23/14.

02409.Name_Class: Salusin-beta (natural AMPs; human;  primates, mammals, animals)
02409.Additional_info: Most similar to AP784: fish NRC-10 (~42% similarity). Active against Gram-positive microorganisms such as B. subtilis NBRC 3513, B. megaterium ATCC 19213, S. aureus NBRC 12732, and S. epidermidis NBRC 12933. Reg6/11/2014.

02408.Name_Class: Lactocin 63 (natural AMPs; bacteriocin;  UCLL1c; Gram-positive bacteria, prokaryotes; XXA)
02408.Additional_info:
APD analysis reveals this sequence is most similar (45.45%) to

02411.Name_Class: Balteatide (natural AMPs; frogs, amphibians, animals; XXA; UCLL1c)
02411.Additional_info: 61.53% sequence similarity to AP905, Hyposin-H4. Active against the yeast C. albicans (MIC 27 uM), and weakly against the Gram-negative bacterium, E. coli (MIC 109 uM). Reg 6/17/2014.

02412.Name_Class: Brevinin-2R (natural AMPs; frogs, amphibians, animals; XXU; 1S=S, UCSS1a)
02412.Additional_info:
Activity: Active against S. aureus, M. luteus, Bacillus spKR-8104, E. coli, S. typhimurium, P. aeruginosa, K. pneumonidae and fungi, such as C. albicans and C. tropicalis.

Toxicity: Brevinin-2R shows higher toxicity towards cancer cells (Jurkat, BJAB, MCF-7, L929, A549) than normal cells. Sheep erythrocytes (RBC): 2.5% hemolysis at 200 ug/ml (little hemo.lytic).

02410.Name_Class: Tolworthcin 524 (natural AMPs; bacteriocins, Gram-positive bacteria, prokaryotes; BWQ, unclassified)
02410.Additional_info: Warning: only partial N-terminal amino acid sequence was obtained. In addition, this partial sequence is identical to the N-terminal region of Thurincin H. Active against B. cereus 183 (233 U), L. mono-cytogenes (13 U), S. aureus (28 U), S. xylosus (63 U), E. faecalis (63 U), Micrococcus sp (126 U) (Gram-positive bacteria), and also against E. cloacae (28 U), K. pneumoniae (264 U), P. aeruginosa (82 U), P. vulgaris (126 U), S. flexneri (63 U), S. sonnei (45 U) (Gram-negative bacteria) as determined by the well-diffusion assay.

02413.Name_Class: Brevinin-1AN1 (XXU; 1S=S, UCSS1a; natural AMPs; frogs, amphibians, animals)
02413.Additional_info:
Activity: Avtive against Gram+ bacteria E.faecium 091299 (IS) (MIC 150 uM), E. faecalis 981 (IS) (MIC 19 uM), S. aureus ATCC25923 (MIC 19 uM), S. carnosus KHS (IS) (MIC 37.5 uM), B. licheniformis X39 (IS) (MIC 37.5 uM), R. rhodochrous X15 (IS)(MIC 4.8 uM), Gram- E.coli ATCC25922 (MIC >150 uM), S.typhi 091408 (IS)(MIC >150 uM), P.aeruginosa (ATCC27853) (MIC >150 uM), P.aeruginosa (ATCC27853) (MIC >150 uM), P. faecalis X29 (IS) (MIC 37.5 uM), and fungi C.albicans ATCC10231 (MIC>150 uM).

Toxicity: hRBC: hemolytic HC50 70 uM. Provided by Biswajit Mishra. Updated 7/2021; 11/2022

02414.Additional_info:

Antimicrobial robustness: Stable to heat treatment (121 oC, 30 min) and pH 4.0–5.0, but not stable to a-Chymotrypsin, trypsin, papain, and pepsin although some stability to protease K was noticed. Updated 8/2014.

02421.Name_Class: Hylaranin-L2  (natural AMPs; frogs, amphibians, animals; XXA; UCLL1c)
02421.Additional_info:
Chemical modification: C-terminal NH2.

Activity: Active against E. coli (MIC 34 uM), S. aureus (MIC 4.3 uM), and C. albicans (MIC 4-9 uM). Need more info here. Reg. 8/2014.

02423.Name_Class: Batroxicidin (BatxC; Vipericidins, Lys-rich; cell-penetrating; natural AMPs; cathelicidins; snake, reptiles, animals)
02423.Additional_info:
Sequence analysis: 91.17% similar to AP897 NA-CATH. Rich in lysines (32%).

Activity: active against Gram+ E. faecalis ATCC 29212 (MIC 7.7-30.8 uM), S. aureus ATCC 29213 (MIC 7.7 uM), S. pyogenes clinical isolate (MIC 3.8 uM), S. aureus (MIC 7.7 uM), Gram- P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853 (MIC 0.2-3.8 uM), K. pneumoniae clinical isolate (MIC 1.9 uM), E. coli ATCC 25922 (MIC 0.06-3.8 uM), and A. baumannii clinical isolate (MIC 3.8 uM). Also active against T. cruzi, a protozoan that causes Chagas' disease (Mello et al., 2017). T. cruzi cell labeling by 7-aminoactinomycin D, the increase in reactive oxygen species and the loss of mitochondrial membrane potential when the parasite was treated with BatxC, which are indication of necrosis.

Appeared to have proinflammatory effect on immune cells such as Raw 264.7 cells (Oliveira-Júnior et al., 2018).

Reg. 8/2014; Updated 3/2017; 11/2023; 12/2024.

02427.Name_Class: CecropinXJ (natural AMPs; insects, arthropods, invertebrates, animals)
02427.Additional_info:
94.59% similar to AP183 cecropin B from the same species.

Activity: Active against Gram-negative bacteria E. coli ATCC 25922 (MIC 1.43 uM), K. pneumoniae (MIC 1.97 uM), S. flexneri (MIC 3.21 uM), A. baumannii (MIC 1.43 uM), S. sonnei (MIC 2.89 uM), K. ozaenae (MIC 4.62 uM), and Gram-positive bacteria S. aureus (MIC 1.81 uM), D. ribution (MIC 2.48 uM), S. epidermidis (MIC 5.76 uM). It also displayed anticancer activity (Xia L et al., 2014).

Recombinant production:yeast:Saccharomyces cerevisiae INVSc1 strain: expressed for 120 h.

02424.Name_Class: Crotalicidin (Ctn, Vipericidins, Lys-rich; natural AMPs; cathelicidins; Rattlesnake, reptiles, animals; derivatives: Ctn[15-34]; more AMPs? Lachesicidin; Lutzicidin )
02424.Additional_info:
Sequence analysis: 85.29% similar to AP896 BF-CATH.

Activity: active against Gram+ E. faecalis ATCC 29212 and a clinical isolate (MIC 7.7-31 uM), S. aureus ATCC 29213 and a clinical isolate (MIC 7.7 uM), S. pyogenes clinical isolate (MIC 3.8 uM), Gram- P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853 and a clinical isolate (MIC 0.24-3.8 uM), K. pneumoniae clinical isolate (MIC 1.9 uM), E. coli ATCC 25922 and a clinical isolate (MIC 0.06-3.8 uM), and A. baumannii clinical isolate (MIC 3.8 uM).

Fungi: active against yeasts C-parapsilosis ATCC 22019 (MIC>40 uM), C. krusei ATCC 6258 (MIC 40 uM), C. tropicalis LABMIC 0109 (MIC 10-40 uM), C. albicans LABMIC 0107 or 0108 (MIC 20-40 uM), C. parapsilosis LABMIC 0113 (MIC 2.5 uM), C. laurentii LABMIC 0404 (MIC 20 uM), Dermatophythes M. canis LABMIC 0401 (MIC 1.25 uM), T. rubrum LABMIC 0203 or 0204 (MIC 5 uM) (Cavalcante et al., 2017).

Appeared to have proinflammatory effect on immune cells such as Raw 264.7 cells (Oliveira-Júnior et al., 2018).

Half-life in vitro:serum:human: half-life 71 min (50% serum).

Structure: residues 3-21 are helical when bound to DPC micelles. You can rotate, zoom, and view the crystal structure of BPTI in complex with trypsin here in the PDB. Ctn is toxic to cancer cells HeLa S3 and U937, in the low uM range for THP-1 (IC50 ~1.56 uM) and MM6 (IC50 3.12 uM), and above 12.5 uM for HL-60 and Jurkat E6.1.

SAR: Like LL-37, the N-terminal fragment Ctn[1-14] has weak activity, while the c-terminal fragment Ctn[15-34] is antibacterial and antitumor with increased cell selectivity (Falcao CB et al., 2015).

Toxicity: Ctn was the most active peptide against dermatophytes. Toxic to human fibroblasts (IC50 6.25 uM) and also the most toxic to healthy eukaryotic cells. Human RBC: HC50 < 100 uM. Fragments Ctn[1–14] and Ctn[15–35] lost activity against dermatophytes, but became more active against pathogenic yeasts, including several Candida species, both clinical isolates and standard strains, with MICs as low as 5 uM (Cavalcante CS et al., 2016).

Synergy:drug: it showed synergistic antifungal activity with amphotericin B (FICI 0.26) (Cavalcante et al., 2017).

Reg. 8/2014; Update 4/2016; 11/2016; 7/2021; 12/2024 GW.
02424.Activity: Anti-Gram+ & Gram-, Antifungal, Synergistic AMPs, Hemolytic, Anticancer

02422.Name_Class: Lc-def (L. culinaris defensin, natural AMPs; dimer, UCSS1a; 4S=S, plants; BBMm)
02422.Additional_info:
Molecular form: Dimer was observed using non-reducing SDS-gel.

Activity: Active against fungi A. niger, strain VKM F-2259 (IC50 18.5 uM), A. versicolor, strain VKM F-1114 (IC50 18.5 uM), B. cinerea, strain VKM F-3700 (IC50 9.25 uM), F. culmorum, strain VKM F-844 (IC50 18.5-37 uM), and N. crassa, strain VKM F-184 (IC50 9.25-18.5 uM).

Structure: Structure was determined by NMR. There are one helical region (residues N21-K27) and three beta strands (K1-L6, S32-C35, and C41-C47). You can rotate, zoom, and view the NMR structure 2LJ7 here in the PDB. However, no spin systems were found for residues C14-C20, probably due to micro-ms time scale motion in the loop regions, which may be involved in membrane targeting. Updated Jan2015.

02426.Name_Class: RNase 6 (Ribonuclease 6; Ribonuclease family, antimicrobial protein; natural AMPs; mouse; rodents, mammals, animals; UCSS1a; 4S=S,)
02426.Additional_info:
The amino acid sequence is 47.28% similar to AP2425 human RNase 6.

Activity: Active against uropathogenic E. coli (UPEC), E. faecalis, and S. saprophyticus at micromolar concentrations.

Recombinant production:bacteria:Escherichia coli: expressed in the BL21 AI strain and purified from inclusion bodies and refolded via dialysis. Updated 8/2023; Jan2024

02428.Name_Class: MtDef4 (M. Truncatula defensin 4, natural AMPs; UCSS1a; 4S=S, plants; BBribo)
02428.Additional_info:
Activity: Active against fungus F. graminearum that causes head blight disease in cereals.

Structure: You can rotate, zoom, and view the NMR structure 2LR3 here in the PDB.

MOA:fungi: MtDef4 binds to phosphatidic acid (PA). PA is a precursor for lipid biosynthesis and a signaling molecule that recruits cytosolic proteins to membranes. MtDef4 rapidly permeabilizes fungal plasma membrane and is internalized by the fungal cells where it accumulates in the cytoplasm (see the structure paper PDB). Since the peptide can enter the cell, new evidence points at inhibition of protein synthesis of ribosome:MOA:fungi:B. cinerea (Li et al., 2024).

SAR: The sequence RGFRRR is likely the translolcation signal. Note that amino acid substitutions in the RGFRRR sequence not only abolished the ability of MtDef4 to enter fungal cells but also impaired its ability to bind PA. Updated 3/2015; 12/2019; 8/2023; 4/2024.

02425.Name_Class: RNase 6 (Ribonuclease 6; RNase6; Ribonuclease family, antimicrobial protein; natural AMPs; human;  primates, mammals, animals; UCSS1a; 4S=S)
02425.Additional_info:
AMP Significance: Rnase6 deficiency (i.e., Rnase6EGFP/EGFP) resulted in increased upper urinary tract UPEC burden during experimental UTI, compared to Rnase6+/+ controls (Cortado et al., 2024).

Discovery: The amino acids sequence was reported by Dyer KD et al. 2004 (J Mol Evol. 2004 Nov; 59:657-65). 39.53% similar to AP2073 RNase 7. Host expression:induced: The expression of this AMP is inducible.

Activity: In 2014, the Spencer lab demonstrated its antimicrobial activity against uropathogenic E. coli (UPEC), E. faecalis, and S. saprophyticus at micromolar concentrations, comparable to RNase 7.

SAR: This peptide has stronger antibacterial activity (e.g., E. coli), LPS binding and bacteria-agglutinating ability compared to a natural variant with a glutamine at position 66 (Refer to AP04036).

Recombinant production:bacteria:Escherichia coli: expressed in the BL21 AI strain and purified from inclusion bodies and refolded via dialysis. The recombinant peptide has a sequence corresponding to the sequence of the native peptide (personal communication to Dr. Spencer).

Structure: You can rotate, zoom, and view the 3D structure here in the PDB.

Update 4/2016; 8/2023; Jan2024; 5/2024; 2/2025.

02429.Name_Class: Plantaricin ZJ5 (PZJ5, natural AMPs; bacteriocin; Gram-positive bacteria, prokaryotes)
02429.Additional_info:
37% similar to Warnericin RK (AP2104). Mass difference suggests post-translational modification fo this peptide yet to be determined.

Activity: Active against L. plantarum, L. monocytogenes, B. subtilis, M. luteus, P. putida, and E. coli. The peptide activity was lost by treatment with pepsin and proteinase K (62%) but not affected by lipase or alpha-amylase. Registered 9/1/2014.

02430.Additional_info:
The APD found 40% similarity to temporin-La.

However, the reduced form of this peptide was found to be more active and M. luteus, L. monocytogenes, and V. cholera were most sensitive.The structure was predicted as a 2-stranded beta-sheet. Reg. 9/2014.

02434.Name_Class: Mytichitin-CB (UCSS1a; 3S=S, natural AMPs; mollusca/molluscs/mollusks, marine invertebrates, animals)
02434.Additional_info: Activity: Primarily active against B. subtilis, S. aureus, S. luteus; and B. megaterium (MIC < 5uM), fungi C. albicans and M. albican (MIC 6.2-25 uM). Only weakly active against V. Parahaemolyticus and P. aeruginosa (MIC 50-100 uM). Reg. 9/2014.

02435.Name_Class: Ponericin-Q42  (natural AMPs; insects, arthropods, invertebrates, animals, UCLL1a)
02435.Additional_info: Activity: Active against A. globiformis VKM Ac-1112, B. subtilis VKM B-501, E. coli MH1 (MIC 0.2-0.6 uM), E. coli DH5a, and P. aeruginosa PAO1 (MIC 5-10 uM). It is unusual that The peptide was shown to be partially helical in water. updated 12/2014.

02433.Name_Class: Carnolysin (natural AMPs; two-component lantibiotic, bacteriocin,  UCSS2b; Gram-positive bacteria, prokaryotes; XTT6; XXW5; XXD6)
02433.Additional_info:
This is a two-component lantibiotic. The sequence of Carnolysin A1 is provided in the sequence field. The sequence of Carnolysin A2 is GDVMPESTPICAGFATLMSSIGLVKTIKGKC. Both sequences are processed after post-translation. Altogether, there are six dehydrated ser or thr, and five thioether bonds in the two chains. For Carnolysin A1, residues 8, 10, and 25 are dehydrated; thioether bonds exist between residues 9, 13; 24,28; 41,45; residues 16, 21, 33, 36, are D-amino acids. For Carnolysin A2, residues 8, 16, and 20 are dehydrated; thioether bonds exist between 7, 11; 26, 31; residues 16 and 19 are D-amino acids, which is the first D-Abu in ribosomally synthesized peptide (Lohans CT et al. 2014). However, further processing appeared to be required to generate active peptides, for example, digestion with endoproteinase GluC.

Activity: The digested peptides were active against L. lactis, E. faecium, and C. maltaromaticum. Reg. 9/18/2014.

02436.Name_Class: MsSN-1 (MsSN1; Alfalfa snakin-1, natural AMPs; plants; UCSS1a; 6S=S)
02436.Additional_info:
This peptide was found from alpalfa, an ancient plant of ~8000 years old, which is good for agriculture.

Activity: Active against P. fluorescens Pf-5, B. japonicum USDA110, M. loti MAFF303099, R. etli CFN 42, S. medicae WSM419, and S. fredii USDA 257.

Recombinant production:plants:Medicago sativa: Transgenic plants: MsSN1-overexpressing transgenic plants showed nodule production of S. meliloti BL225C comparable with that of the wild type plants.

Reg. 9/23/2014.

02438.Name_Class: SRTAP-40 (natural AMPs; sheep, ruminant, mammals; animals)
02438.Additional_info:
APD analysis showed 32.5% sequence similary to cPcAMP1/26. Mol. Wt, 4911.741; Mol formula, C230H355N55O61S1; GRAVY, -0.27; Wimley-White whole-residue hydrophobicity, 8.2 kcal/mol.

Activity: Active against E. coli ATCC25922 (MIC 12 ug/ml), S. aureus ATCC25923 (MIC 12 ug/ml), Streptococcus sp. ATCC55121 (MIC 24 ug/ml) and C. albicans ATCC2002 (MIC 6 ug/ml). These are MIC50. Reg. 9/2014; SEQ updated 8/2017. GW.

02437.Additional_info:
41.6% similar to Phylloseptin-H9 and NRC-10. The peptide was identified from Trichoplax adhaerens, the only described species in the phylum Placozoa, structurally simplest multicellular animal.

Activity: Active against Gram+ S. aureus (MRSA), L. ivanovii (MIC 3 uM), E. faecalis (MIC 12.5 uM), Gram- bacteria E. coli ATCC 25922, P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853, A. baumannii ATCC 19606, K. pneumoniae ATCC 13883 (MIC 3-6 uM), fungi C. albicans ATCC 90028 and C. parapsilosis ATCC 22019 (MIC 25-50 uM). This peptide showed a relatively good cell selectivity index (65-260). Trichoplaxin is random in water but helical in the presence of membrane-mimetic models such as SDS or TFE. Reg. 9/2014; 12/2014.

02441.Name_Class: S. amritsarensis lipopeptide (natural AMPs; nonribosomal peptide, bacteria, prokaryotes; XXL)
02441.Additional_info:

Antimicrobial robustness: Stable to heat (70oC, 1 h or autoclaving 121oC 15 min), trypsin,proteinase K and lipase enzymes.

02442.Name_Class: PcALF1 (P. clarkii  anti-lipopolysaccharide factor 1; natural AMPs; Crustaceans, arthropods, invertebrates, animals;1S=S; UCSS1; BBL; BBS)
02442.Additional_info: Activity: Active against G+ bacteria S. aureus, B. subtilis, B. cereus, B. thuringiensis, and B. megaterium, G- bacteria E. coli and P. aeruginosa, including V. anguillarum, and fungi C. albicans. Recombinant PcALF1 can clear fish pathogen V. anguillarum.

02440.Name_Class: Copsin (defensin; natural AMPs; fungi,fungii; UCSS1a; 6S=S; XXQ; BBW)
02440.Additional_info:
Activity: Active against B. subtilis 168; S. pneumoniae, S. pyogenes, S. carnosus, S. epidermidis, L. monocytogenes WSLC 1042 or 1001, L. ivanovii WSLC 3009 or 2012, E. faecium DSM 20477, E. faecium VRE DSM 13590 (anti-VRE), E. faecalis DSM 20478, M. luteus, C. diphtheriae.

Structure: The N-terminal Q is a pyroglutamate (XXQ). You can rotate, zoom, and view the 3D structure here in the PDB. The 3D structure has two antiparallel beta regions and two helical regions (see PDB annotation, Sequence). In addition, there are 6 disulfide bonds: C3-C32; C10-C40; C18-48; C22-C50; C25-C57; and C35-C54 that stabilize this small protein fold.

MOA: copsin appears to inhibit bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to lipid II.

Recombinant production:bacteria: activity testing using recombinant peptide.

02444.Name_Class: EsALF-1 (E. sinensis anti-lipopolysaccharide factor 2; natural AMPs; Crustaceans, arthropods, invertebrates, animals;1S=S; BBL)

02445.Name_Class: P. sarana Hepcidin (Cys-rich; natural AMPs; fish, animals; UCSS1a; 4S=S)

02446.Name_Class: Haliotisin peptide 3-4-5 (natural AMPs; mollusca/molluscs/mollusks, marine invertebrates, animals)

02448.Name_Class: CPF-RP-F1 (natural AMPs; frogs, amphibians, animals; XXA; UCLL1c)

02447.Name_Class: Scolopendin 2 (natural AMPs; myriapods, arthropods, invertebrates, animals)
02447.Additional_info:
Activity: Active against Gram+ E. faecium ATCC 19434 (MIC 12.5 uM), S. aureus ATCC 25923 (MIC 25 uM), and MRSA (MIC 12.5 uM), Gram- bacteria E. coli O157 ATCC 43895 (MIC 6.3 uM), S. typhi ATCC 19430 (MIC 12.5 uM), P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853 including three resistant strains (MIC 6.3-12.5 uM), and fungi C. albicans ATCC 90028 (MIC 6.3 uM), C. parapsilosis ATCC 22019 (MIC 12.5 uM), T. beigelii KCTC 7707 (MIC 6.3 uM), and T. rubrum KCTC 6345 (MIC 6.3 uM).

MOA: The peptide caused permeabilization and depolarization of membranes. It induced calcein release from vesicles. It also induced potassium leakage after treatment of E. coli or C. albicans, implying formation of pore at a size 4.8-5.0 nm.

Structure: it is random in buffer but helical in membrane-mimetic TFE, SDS, or DPC.

Toxicity: not hemo.lytic at 100 uM. Cf. Melittin showed 100% lyss at 12.5 uM.

Updated 7/2021

02449.Name_Class: Magainin-F3 (natural AMPs; frogs, amphibians, animals; UCLL1; More AMPs?)

02450.Name_Class: Ala-6-fenycin (BLIS P34, natural AMPs; Glu-rich; lactone, depsipeptide, lipopeptide, XXL; XXJ; UCSB1b; nonribosomal peptide, bacteria, prokaryotes; Various lipidated forms)
02450.Additional_info:
BLIS: bacteriocin-like inhibitory substances. An acyl chain (C15 to C17 carbons) is attached to E1, residue 2 is an ornithine (represented as K), and the carboxylic group of C-terminal I10 forms an ester bond with the side chain of Y3.

Activity: Active against Gram-positive bacteria (B. subtilis, L. acidophilus ATCC 4356, B. linens, C. Wmi NCTC 7547, L. monocytogenes, L. innocua, B. cereus, L. innocua ATCC 33090, L. innocua 1572, L. ivanovii 5 NCTC 11007, L. seeligeri AC 82/4, L. welshimeri AC 73/2, (Motta et al., 2007b), and Gram-negative bacteria (S. Gallinarum, E. carotovora 413, A. hydrophila, P. haemolytica, P. haemolytica, clinical isolate). Also inhibited the replication of viruses such as equine arteritis virus (EAV) and feline herpesvirus type 1 (FHV-1) by over 94%. Updated 9/2017.

02451.Name_Class: Eotaxin-2 (CCL24, CCL-24, cytokine, CC family; kinocidins; UCSS1a; 2S=S, natural AMPs; human,  primates, mammals, animals; variants)

The primary structure was reported in 1997 by Forssmann U and colleagues. Three C-terminal truncated variants with 73, 75, and 76 residues were isolated as well. NMR structure (73 residues) was solved in 2000 (go to the PDB link). You can rotate, zoom, and view the 3D structure here in the PDB. Reg 12/10/2014.

02453.Name_Class: Scolopendin 1 (natural AMPs; myriapods, arthropods, invertebrates, animals; XXA)

02520.Name_Class: Enterocin O16 (EntV; natural AMPs; bacteriocins; Gram-positive bacteria, prokaryotes)
02520.Additional_info:
AMP Significance: In the gastrointestinal and oral microbiome, both Enterococcus faecalis and Candida albicans co-exist and antagonize each other. Interestingly, Enterococcus faecalis can secret the same bacteriocin (named EntV) to inhibit C. albicans and its biofilm formation (Brown et al., 2019).

Sequence analysis: 36.25% SIMILAR TO

Enterocin O16 includes the C-terminal 68 residues of the EF1097 precursor protein. The protease GelE is responsible for the release of this bacteriocin. With two Cys residues, there may be a disulfide bond.

Activity: A narrow-spectrum peptide with MIC in the range of nM. Active against L. sakei LMG 2313 or LMG 3354 or LMG 3355 or LMG 3356 or LMG 3357 (MIC 0.5-500 ng/ml), and L. plantarum LMG 2003 (MIC 31 ng/ml).

Structure: determined using single anomalous dispersion (SAD) phasing to 1.8 Å resolution. There are seven helical regions in the crystal structure.

Animal model:Caenorhabditis elegans: 0.1 nM EntV completely protected nematode Caenorhabditis elegans from C. albicans infection, and increased fungal clearance by murine macrophages (Graham et al., 2017).

Half-life in vitro:serum: about 10% remaining after 4 h of incubation in 10% serum.

SAR: a 12mer of the alpha7 helix, retaining a full three turns of the alpha-helix and ending with cysteine-167, is as effective in protecting against C. albicans infection in the worm model and inhibiting surface adhesion as full-length EntV. The active fragments of helix 7 are also registered into the APD (Cruz et al., 2022).

Recombinant production:bacteria:Escherichia coli: The peptide was expressed and purifed for SAR studies.

Updated 7/2019; SAR 5/2024.

02534.Name_Class: sPLA2-IIA  (secreted type IIA Phospholipase A2, antimicrobial protein; natural AMPs; human, primates, mammals, animals; 7S=S; UCSS1a)
02534.Additional_info: APD analysis reveals that the sequence is 21% similar to Crustacean PtALF3. Active against Gram-positive S. aureus, P. aeruginosa, B. anthracis, and P. aeruginosa (Wu Y et al., 2010). Antibacterial effect against P. aeruginosa using recombinant protein was not affected by high salt concentrations (salt-insensitive) (Dubouix A et al., 2003). The positive charge of the protein is demonstrated to be important for binding to negatively charged cell wall of S. aureus (Koprivnjak T et al., 2002). You can rotate, zoom, and view the 3D structure here in the PDB. Of outstanding interest is Pseudomanas aeruginosa can induce the expression of sPLA2-IIA that is sufficient to kill S. aureus in CF airways. This discovery explains the shift of the predominant bacterium in CF lung from S. aureus observed in young patients to Pseudomanas aeruginosa in adults (Pernet E et al., 2014). Additional data are required how these bacteria escape the killing of human AMPs. In the early stage, S. aureus appears to use adenosine to inhibit phagocytosis and sPLA2-IIA expression (Pernet E eta l., 2015). Animal model:mouse: Instillation of recombinant sPLA2-IIA to infected mice can circumvent inhibition of endogenous sPLA2-IIA expression by anthrax toxins, thereby protecting mice from death due to B. anthracis infection. Updated 4/2014; 8/2015 GW.

02570.Name_Class: GL13K (a derivative of GL13NH2; Lys-rich; Leu-rich; BBL; BBMm; XXA; UCLL1c; synthetic AMPs20; Derivative: DGL13K)
02570.Additional_info:
APD analysis reveals that the sequence of GL13K most resembles (53.8%) frog PGLa-H.

Structure: Interestingly, CD spectra suggest a beta structure in liposomes containing aninoic lipid PGs (Balhara V et al., 2013). Note that the peptide is random coil in water, but adopted a helical structure in DPC, indicating structural plasticity.

Design: GL13K is obtained by substituting 3 residues (Q2, N5, and D11) of GL13NH2 with lysines. The PSP (Parotid secretory protein) peptide GL13NH2 (sequence GQIINLKASLDLL), which corresponds to a lipopolysaccharide-inhibiting peptide from LBP, binds lipopolysaccharides (BBL) and agglutinated bacteria. GL13NH2 is a potential dual-function host defense salivary protein with agglutination (bacteria-agglutinating) and anti-inflammatory activity (Gorr SU et al. 2011), but it did not kill bacteria.

Activity: Its lysine analog, GL13K, however, is active against P. aeruginosa (MIC 8 ug/ml), E. coli (MIC 5 ug/ml), S. gordonii (MIC 64 ug/ml) and S. aureus (MIC 41 ug/ml) (Harmouche N et al., 2017).

GL13K also has antibiofilm activity against P. aeruginosa (Hirt and Gorr, 2013).

SAR The D-form of this peptide is more potent and took bacteira additional time to develop resistance.

Toxicity: It has low hemolytic activity.

Animal model:mouse: GL13K protects mice from LPS-induced sepsis (Abdolhosseini M et al. 2012). DGL13K (made of D-amino acids) killed P. aeruginosa in both the G. mellonella model (animal model:wax moth) and a mouse burn wound infection model (animal model:mouse), with bacterial viability 3-10-fold lower than in untreated controls.

Resistance development:yes:bacteria:P. gingivalis: P. gingivalis W50 was resistant to LGL13K (L-form) but susceptible to the all-D-amino acid stereoisomer, DGL13K. DGL13K can defeat multiple bacterial resistance mechanisms but bacteria can gain tolerance to DGL13K through mutations in the hagA gene (Gorr et al., 2024).

Surface immobilized peptides: Surface coating (titanium) of GL13K conferred antimicrobial activity and reduced bacteria CFU, a tech with potential application in dental care (Holmberg KV et al., 2013).

Peptide formulation: it has been loaded to thermosensitive hydrogel for prolonged release (2 wks) on a titanium surface to improve its antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties (Zhou et al., 2023).

Deposited and provided by Sven-Ulrik Gorr 6/2015; updated 11/2017; 8/2023; 10/2024 GW.

02579.Name_Class: Defensin 1 (natural AMPs; insects, arthropods, invertebrates, animals; 3S=S; UCSS1a; JJsn)
02579.Additional_info:

Activity: E. coli Active against S. aureus MW2, USA100, USA300, USA400, RN4220, Newman, and clinical isolates including BF1,BF5, BF7 to BF11 and S. epidermidis 9142 (MIC 16-64 ug/ml). Of the 23 AMPs tested, only this peptide is effective against S. pneumoniae D39 (Lindhauer et al., 2019).

Synergy:AMPs: It showed synergistic effects with telavancin (synergy2) and daptomycin (synergy1).

Antimicrobial robustness: Activity can be compromised by salts: NaCl-sensitive:S. aureus MW2 (50-100 mM); CaCl2-sensitive:S. aureus MW2 (1.25-100 mM).

Animal model:Caenorhabditis elegans: it showed dose-dependent protection of animal survival against MRSA.

02580.Additional_info:
APD analysis reveals that the sequence of BG-CATH37 shows 39.1% similarity to Bovine Beta-defensin 11.

Activity: active against habitat bacteria A. hydrophila (MIC 40 ug/ml), V. splendidus (MIC 6.25 ug/ml), and S. iniae (MIC 12.5 ug/ml), but inactive: E.coli ATCC 25922, P.aeruginosa ATCC 27853, and S.aureus ATCC 25923 (MIC >200 ug/ml). An alternative cleaved form of the peptide is BG-CATH(5-37), which lacks the N-terminal 4 residues of BG-CATH37, is also active against these bacteria (gram- A. hydrophila, MIC 12.5 ug/ml; V. splendidus, MIC 3.1 ug/ml; Gram+ S. iniae, MIC 12.5 ug/ml). Which one corresponds to the native mature peptide remains to be established via isolation from the toad.

Toxicity: Notably, synthetic forms of these peptides showed no hemo.lytic activity at 400 ug/mL.

Structure: CD showed mainly random coils in water or in the presence of SDS or TFE. Updated 7/2021

Activity: Active against a panel of Gram-positive bacteria, L. lactis ssp. lactis ATCC 19435, L. lactis ssp. lactis IL1403, L. lactis ssp. cremoris NZ9000, L. lactis ssp. lactis JCM 7638, Lactococcus sp. QU 12, Lactobacillus sakei ssp. sakei JCM 1157, L. plantarum JCM 14917, Leu. mesenteroides TK41401, Leu. mesenteroides ssp. mesenteroides JCM 6124, P. pentosaceus JCM 5890, P. dextrinicus JCM 5887, E. faecium JCM 5804, E. faecalis JCM 5803, E. faecalis NKR-4-1, E. faecalis JH-2-2, E. faecium NKR-5-3, S. bovis JCM 5802, B. coagulans JCM 2257, B. circulans JCM 2504, B. subtilis JCM 1465, K. rhizophila NBRC 12708, L. innocua ATCC 33090, L. monocytogenes ATCC BAA-679, and S. epidermidis JCM 2414 (MIC 0.05-5.7 uM).

Structure: Structurally, it is highly similar to carnocyclin A. You can rotate, zoom, and view the 3D structure here in the PDB. In addition, the charge distribution of enterocin NKR-5-3B, carnocyclin A and enterocin AS-48 are also highly conserved (Himeno et al., 2015).

Recombinant production:bacteria: Heterologous production of Ent53B through the pNK-B1234 expression plasmid by Lactococcus lactis ATCC 19435T, IL1403 and NZ9000 host strains under chloramphenicol selection (Perez et al., 2015).

Peptide stability: stable against thermal, chemical and proteolytic degradation (Wang et al., 2023).

Updated 12/2015; 8/2023.

02628.Name_Class: Jaburetox-2Ec (jbtx; a fragment of canatoxin, a urease isoform; natural AMPs; plants; pepcanatox; UCLL1a)
02628.Additional_info: APD analysis reveals that the sequence of this peptide most resembles (43.6% similarity) Mj-AMP2. Mol Wt: 10098.318; mol formula: C440H690N114O147S5; GRAVY: -0.53. Its toxicity relies on an internal 10 kDa peptide (pepcanatox), released by hydrolysis of Canatoxin by cathepsins in the digestive system of susceptible insects. Shown here is the 93 amino acid fragment recombinantly expressed for biological and structural analysis (The six-residue His tag was omitted). It is insecticidal (e.g. S. frugiperda larvae). In 2012, it was shown to also inhibit fungi such as S. cerevisiae, C. parapsilosis, P. membranisfaciens at 9 uM and yeasts, C. tropicalis, K. marxiannus and C. albicans at 18 uM (Postal M et al., 2012). Membane permeation is the likely mechanism for inhibiting both insects and fungi. It seems that the N-terminal 44 residues are more important than the C-terminal portion (Martinelli AH et al., 2014). A helical region was found at the N-terminus. However, the peptide is largely diosordered, consistent with (15)N relaxation studies that revealed significant backbone mobility, especially in the N-terminal portion of the polypeptide (Lopes FC et al., 2015).

MOA:bacteria:E. coli: depolarized membranes.

Structure: random coill in PBS, helical in 30 mM SDS or 50% TFE.

In vitro toxicity: human RBC: highly hemolytic: the peptide displayed 50% hemolysis at 8-20 uM (no serum) and 32 uM in the presence of 10% fetal calf serum (FBS).

SAR: Two fragments dCATH(1-16) and dCATH(5-20) showed broad activity against both Gram+ and Gram- pathogens (MIC 2-8 uM) in the presence of physiolocal concentrations of salts. These fragments are less toxic. A change of W4 to A, or W17 to A substantially reduced peptide activities. The fragments bind LPS and suppress the release of TNF-alpha, IL-6, and NO from RAW 264.7 cells, implying an anti-inflammatory effect (Feng et al., 2020).

Animal model:mouse: bacteremia:(S. aureus infection, penisin at 80 mg/kg efficiently protected 80% of the BALB/c mice, which survived even after 8 days.

Discovery: It can only be expressed when the bacterium was grown on solid culture medium. Chromatigraphic purification, including HPLC.

02645.Name_Class: PvHCt (classic His-rich classic; fragment of hemocyanin, natural AMPs; metallo-AMPs; shrimp, Crustaceans, arthropods, invertebrates, animals; BBMm; UCLL1a)
02645.Additional_info:
Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that the sequence of this peptide most resembles (44.4% similarity) fish NRC-19. H: 22%, F: 13%.

Activity: It inhibits the spore germination of the shrimp pathogen F. oxysporum.

Antimicrobial robustness: Activity is salt-insensitive.

Structure: In complex with DPC (1:100, P/L ratio, pH 3.5), it is helical from residues 6-18 determined by solution NMR. You can rotate, zoom, and view the 3D structure here in the PDB.

MOA:bacteria: Three phenylalanines are aligned on the hydrophobic surface and can play an important role in membrane targeting as previously demonstrated for human LL-37.

Metal binding:Cu: copper Cu(II) binds to the central (H9 and H17) and C-terminal regions of the peptide, causing structural changes, increased helical content, and ROS production (Miller et al., 2025). However, Metal binding:Zn: Zn(II) only binds to the C-terminus and showed minimal effects on structure. However, Zn binding increased activity against MRSA (provided by authors).

Peptide production:protein cleavage: Since it corresponds to the C-terminal fragment of hemocyanin, it can be obtained in large quantities by proteolytic cleavage of the protein.

Updated 11/2025

Biotech. and Agrochem, Tokyo, pp. 703-705),

02671.Additional_info:
Discovery: A short cecropin A-melittin hybrid peptide obtained by optimizing BP76 (sequence: KKLFKKILKFL). Other peptides with an optimal balance between antibacterial and hemolytic activities include BP66, BP77, BP81, BP105, BP125, and BP126 (see the ref).

Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that the sequence of BP100 most resembles (66.7% similarity) CM15.

Activity: Highly active against E. amylovora (MIC 2.5-5.0 uM), X. axonopodis pv. vesicatoria (MIC 5.0-7.5 uM), and P. syringae pv. syringae (MIC 2.5-5.0 uM).

This peptide appears to have cell penetrating property (Eggenberger et al., 2011).

MOA:bacteria:E. coli: it damaged bacterial membranes (Alves et al, 2010).

Toxicity: exhibited low hemo.lytic activity (HC50>150 uM; 22% at 150 uM).

Plant model:flowers: BP100 is highly active to prevent infections of plant pathogen E. amylovora in apple and pear flowers. It is only slightly less potent than streptomycin used in blight control.

SAR: Another paper investigated the impact of D-amino acid incorporation, e.g. BP143 (a D-AA at position 4) and BP145 (a D-AA at position 2) (Guell et al., 2011). Peptide BP143 was as effective as streptomycin in the three pathosystems, was more effective than BP100 against bacterial blight of pepper and pear, and equally effective against fire blight of pear.

Plant protection:apple: Plant protection:pear: flowers pretreated at 100 and 200 uM of BP100 reduced the infection of plant pathogen E. amylovora.

Recombinant production:plants:Oryza sativa: Transgenic plants: expressed in transgenic rice cells (Company et al., 2014).

These include B. cereus (MIC 16 uM), B. pumilus (MIC 16 uM), B. megaterium (MIC 16 uM), B. coagulans (MIC 16 uM), B. subtilis (MIC 16 uM), G. stearothermophilus (MIC 32 uM), A. acidoterrestris (MIC 16 uM), P. polymyxa (MIC 16 uM), C. difficile (MIC 32 uM), C. perfringens (MIC 32 uM), C. sporogenes (MIC 32 uM), S. aureus (MIC 16 uM), M. luteus (MIC 16 uM), P. fluorescens (MIC 16 uM), S. marcescens (MIC 16 uM), E. coli (MIC 64 uM), S. enteritidis (MIC 16 uM), S. typhimurium (MIC 32 uM), S. paratyphi A (MIC 16 uM), S. paratyphi B (MIC 16 uM), S. flexneri (MIC 32 uM), and P. mirabilis (MIC 16 uM). Thus, plantaricin JLA-9 has potential applications in the control of Bacillus spp. in the food industry. Updated 7/2021

Thus, the first two arginines are essential for the bactericidal activity of hLF against these bacteria. In addition, hLF(1-11) is at least 10 times more potent than hLF(21-31), another cationic region of human lactoferrin.

Surface immobilized peptides: hLF1-11 has been covalently immobilized 2014 to the titanium surface to reduces bacterial adhesion and biofilm formation (Godoy-Gallardo M et al., 2014).

Animal model:rabbit:contact lens induced peripheral ulcers (CLPUs): S. aureus infected, resulted in significant reductions in ocular symptom scores and in the extent of corneal infiltration (P < 0.05).

Animal model:mouse: Animal model:rat: titanium-covalently coated surfaces reduced bacterial load in subcutaneous infection by 2 logs (Chen et al., 2016).

Clinical trials:immobilized AMPs: phase III trials for the prevention of keratitis infection with extended-wear contact lenses.

Activity: Active against B. cereus, B. firmus, B. thuringiensis, B. subtilis, B. pumilus, E. faecalis, M. Paenibacillus, S. aureus, and S. sciuri. This peptide can be further modified into thuricin 4A-4D, which may result from succinylation at a lysine residue.

02728.Name_Class: Sviceucin (natural AMPs; lactam;  class 1 lasso peptides; XXJ; 2S=S, UCSB1a; bacteriocin; Gram-positive bacteria, prokaryotes)
02728.Additional_info:
Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows poor sequence similarity (52.2%) to siamycin.

Chemical modification: S-S bonds: C1-C13 and C7-C19.

Activity: Sviceucin showed moderate activity against Gram+ bacteria BUT NOT Gram- bacteria or fungi. Most sensitive strains include B. megaterium, L. bulgaricus 340, S. aureus ATCC 6538, L. sakei subsp. sakei DSM 20017, and a closely related Streptomyces sp. 523 (MIC 1.25-2.5 uM).

Structure: You can rotate, zoom, and view the lipid II bound 3D structure here in the PDB. Updated Jan2017.

02729.Name_Class: Smp24 (natural AMPs; scorpions, arachnids, Chelicerata, arthropods, invertebrates, animals; UCLL1a)
02729.Additional_info:
APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows poor sequence similarity (52%) to Scorpion VpAmp2.0.

Activity: Active against B. subtilis NCIMB 8024, S. epidermidis sp., S. aureus SH100 (MIC 4-8 ug/ml), E. coli JM109 (MIC 64 ug/ml), and C. albicans (MIC 32 ug/ml).

Structure: The peptide can adopt a helical conformation in 60% TFE, laying a basis for memrbane targeting.

Toxicity: it showed toxicity to mammalian cells (cancer or non-cancer).

MOA:cancer: The peptide appears to activate a cascade of events leading to cell death via inducing caspase-1 dependent pyroptosis as indicated by the release of IL-1beta (Elrayess et al., 2022). Removal of the N-terminal four residues increases peptide cell selectivity. Updated 9/2016; Jan2022

02727.Name_Class: Lacrain (natural AMPs; myriapods, arthropods, invertebrates, animals; UCLL1a)
02727.Additional_info:
APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows poor sequence similarity (44.4%) to EP3.

Activity: Active against P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853, A. faecalis ATCC 8750, S. marcescens ATCC 4112, E. cloacae beta-12, S. serovars. S. enterica subsp. arizonae, E. coli SBS363, and E. coli D31 (MIC 2.9-5.8 ug/mL). Updated 12/30/2018.

02725.Name_Class: Thusin (ThsA1, ThsA2; natural AMPs; two-chain lantibiotic, type 2, class 1 bacteriocins; UCSS2b; Gram-positive bacteria, prokaryotes)
02725.Additional_info:
APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows poor sequence similarity (46.2%) to BHT-A1.

Activity: It is active when mixed with another chain (seq: GTPAITTAISAIIAATAQSPCPTSACSKSCNK) at a 1:1 ratio. Active against S. pneumoniae ATCC 49619, B. cereus ATCC 14579, B. thuringiensis BMB171, B. pumilus SCG I , B. subtilis Bsn5, L. monocytogenes LM201 (MIC 6.25 uM), L. monocytogenes LM605, S. aureus ATCC 43300, S. sciuri Bom1, B. amyloliquefaciens X1 (MIC 12.5 uM), S. aureus CMCC 26003, MRSA (MIC 25 uM), and E. faecalis ATCC 29212 (MIC 50 uM).

02731.Name_Class: Panusin (beta defensins; natural AMPs; crustaceans, arthropods, invertebrates, animals; XXA; UCSS1a)
02731.Additional_info:
APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows 40.9% sequence similarity to Bovine beta-defensin 13. Predicted to be a beta defensin.

Activity: Active against E. coli, K. pneumonia, S. aureus, B. subtilis, and C. albicans.

Antimicrobial robustness: Salt-resistant (salt-insensitive). UPdate 10/2022 B. subtilis name corrected by A.P.D.

02732.Name_Class: WB Piscidin 5 (WB P5, natural AMPs; fish, animals; UCLL1a)
02732.Additional_info:

Activity: fish pathogens S. iniae (MIC 2.26-4.52 uM), L. garvieae (MIC 9.03 uM), V. anguillarum (MIC 4.52 uM), A-salmonicida (MIC >36.12 uM), human pathogens E. faecalis (MIC 4.52 uM), S. aureus (MIC 4.52 uM), S. flexneri (MIC 1.13-2.26 uM), and E. coli (MIC 1.13 uM). Its minimum parasiticidal concentrations (PCmin 0.56 uM; PC100 1.10 uM). Updated 4/2024

02730.Name_Class: Smp43 (natural AMPs; scorpions, arachnids, Chelicerata, arthropods, invertebrates, animals; UCLL1a)
02730.Additional_info:
Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows poor sequence similarity (84%) to Scorpion Opistoporin 2.

Activity: Active against B. subtilis NCIMB 8024 (MIC 4 ug/ml), S. epidermidis sp., S. aureus SH100 (MIC 32-64 ug/ml), E. coli JM109, K. pneumoniae NCTC 13439, and C. albicans (MIC 64-128 ug/ml).

Structure: The peptide can adopt a helical conformation in 60% TFE, laying a basis for memrbane targeting.

SAR: Residues 1-14 retains antibacterial activity against both Gram+ and Gram- bacteria, indicating the importance of the N-terminal region (Luo et al., 2021).

in vitro toxicity: it showed toxicity to mammalian cells. The peptide appears to activate a cascade of events leading to cell death via inducing caspase-1 dependent pyroptosis (Elrayess et al., 2022).

MOA:cancer: it damaged Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer A549 Cells via Inducing Membranolysis and Mitochondrial Dysfunction (Deng et al., 2023). Updated 9/2016; 7/2021; 4/2024 GW

02733.Name_Class: WB Piscidin 6  (WB P6, natural AMPs; fish, animals; UCLL1a)
02733.Additional_info:
APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows 35.9% POOR similarity to BmKbpp.

Activity: fish pathogens S-iniae (MIC >31.59 uM), L. garvieae (MIC 0.99 uM), V-anguillarum (MIC >31.59 uM), A-salmonicida (MIC>31.59 uM), human pathogens E-faecalis (MIC >31.59 uM), S-aureus (MIC >31.59 uM), S-flexneri (MIC >31.59 uM), and E-coli (MIC >31.59 uM). Its minimum parasiticidal concentrations (PCmin <0.25 uM; PC100 0.99 uM). Updated 4/2024

02735.Name_Class: Oryctes rhinoceros defensin (UCSS1a; 3S=S, natural AMPs; insects, arthropods, invertebrate, animals)
02735.Additional_info: APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows 86% similarity to A. dichotoma defensin. Active against S. aureus. A syntheic peptide corresponding to the 9 residues close to the C-terminus (AHCLAICRK-NH2) is active against methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), E. coli and P. aeruginosa. Five more 9mers were made and are also active. These peptides show no hemolytic activity and did not inhibit the growth of murine fibroblast cells or macrophages. However, AWLLAIRKR-NH2 is toxic.

02734.Name_Class: SB Piscidin 7 (SB P7, natural AMPs; fish, animals; UCLL1a)

Its minimum parasiticidal concentrations (PCmin <0.25 uM; PC100 1.00 uM).Updated 4/2024

02736.Additional_info: APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows 74.5% similarity to plant defensin MtDef4. Active against S. cerevisiae. Note that antifungal activity is not correlated with channel blocking property of the peptide (Kv1.2 and Kv1.6 potassiumchannel inhibitor).

02737.Name_Class: Labaditin (Lo; natural AMPs; plants; XXC; UCBB1aA)
02737.Additional_info: APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows 40% similarity to bacterial Dosotamide E. Active against S. mutans (ref) and S. aureus. The cyclic structure is critical for antimicrobial activity against S. aureus (Barbosa SC et al., 2016).

02738.Name_Class: Cremycin-5 (natural AMPs; nematode; invertebrates, animals; UCSS1a, 3S=S; more AMPs?)
02738.Additional_info:

Activity: zone diffusion assay: Active against A. niger (CL 14.9 uM), A. nidulans RCho15 or RCho10 or tCho4 (CL 0.7-1.5 uM), G. candidum (CL 4.7 uM), N. crassa (CL 0.6 uM), C. albicans 16 strains (CL 1.8-26 uM), (CL 14.9 uM), C. tropicalis JX1009 or JX1016 or JX1017 (CL 8.8 uM), S. cerevisiae (CL 6.7 uM). 02739.Name_Class: Cremycin-15 (natural AMPs; nematode; invertebrates, animals; UCSS1a, 3S=S)
02739.Additional_info:

02740.Name_Class: Antapin (ANTP; natural AMPs; insects, arthropods, invertebrates, animals; XXA; UCLL1c)
02740.Additional_info: APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows 47.6% similarity to FROG Fallaxidin 4.1. Active against B. subtilis, E. coli, S. aureus, and P. aeruginosa. It became more helical in the presence of TFE, SDS, or anionic lipids.

02741.Name_Class: Formicin (natural AMPs; lantibiotic; two-chain bacteriocins; class 1 bacteriocin; Gram-positive bacteria, prokaryotes; XXW4, XXT7, 1S=S; UCSS2b)
02741.Additional_info:
APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows 71.4% similarity to bacterial 2-chain Haloduracin. Because of this similarity, the connection patterns of sidechains are predicted to be similar (Chain A, FrcA: disulfide bond between C1-C8, lanthionine bridges between S7-C17, T18-C23, and T20-C27; Chain B: lanthionine bridges between T1-C8, T13-C17, S19-C23, T23-C26). In addition, T2, S4, S5, and T10 are dehydrated into Dha or Dhb. Formicin is unique as the chain A is much less hydrophobic but most positively charged than other similar chains; chain B contains a negative charge (sequence: TTPSSLPCGTLVTAVWCPSNACTSDC).

Activity: Active against a broad spectrum of Gram+ bacteria (e.g., L. delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus; L. amylophilus; L. lactis; M. luteus; S. smutans), including clinical strains S. aureus, C. difficile, and L. monocytogenes. Updated 10/2022 bacteria names fixed A.P.D.

02742.Name_Class: Armadillidin Q (Gly-rich; natural AMPs; Terrestrial Isopod, Crustaceans, arthropods,  invertebrates, animals, XXA; BBMm)
02742.Additional_info: APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows 98.1% similarity to Armadillidin H. Rich in glycines (47%). There are six repeated motifs GGGF(H/N)(R/S). Active against B. megaterium F04 (MBC 4.75 uM) and P. syringae DC3000 (MBC 1.18 uM). Very rapid killing started at 30 s and 5 min. Membrane targeting. .

02743.Name_Class: ShLysG (G-type lysozyme, antimicrobial protein; natural AMPs; fish; anaimals; UCLL1)
02743.Additional_info: APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows poor similarity (13.5%) to Cy-AMP3. rShLysG showed greater antimicrobial activity than HEWL towards five fish bacterial pathogens, including V. salmonicida, V. parahaemolyticus, L. monocytogenes, S. iniae,and V. anguillarum.

02744.Name_Class: Saha-CATH3 (natural AMPs; cathelicidins; mammals, animals; UCLL1)
02744.Additional_info:
APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows low similarity (37.8%) to LyeTx I.

Activity: Active against C. neoformans (MIC 16 ug/mL). Also toxic to Devil Facial Tumour Disease (DFTD) cells (Petrohilos et al., 2023). Updated 8/2023.

02745.Name_Class: Saha-CATH5 (natural AMPs; cathelicidins; mammals, animals; UCLL1)

Active against E. coli ATCC 25922, P. aeruginosa, E. faecalis, S. aureus ATCC 29213 (MRSA), S. pneumoniae ATCC 49619, S. pyogenes ATCC 19615, S. agalactiae ATCC 12386, S. agalactiae, S. anginosus, S. equi, and C. neoformans (MIC 32-64 ug/mL).

02748.Name_Class: Ocellatin-PT3 (natural AMPs; frog, amphibians, animals, XXA, UCLL1c)
02748.Additional_info: APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows 84% similarity to Ocellatin-PT4. Originally discovered in 2015, it has leishmanicidal activity (IC50 13.4 uM) (Oliveira M et al., 2016).

02749.Name_Class: Ocellatin-PT6 (natural AMPs; frog, amphibians, animals, UCLL1a)
02749.Additional_info:
Sequence analysis:APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows 96.9% similarity to Ocellatin-PT7.

Activity: Originally discovered in 2015, it has leishmanicidal activity (IC50 12.7 uM) (Oliveira M et al., 2016).

Activity: Weakly active against E.coli ATCC 25922 (MIC 120 uM), K.pneumoniae ATCC 700603 (MIC >240 uM), S.choleraesuis ATCC 14028 (MIC >240 uM), and S.aureus ATCC 29313 (MIC >240 uM).

02750.Name_Class: TLN-58 (TLN58; natural AMPs; alternatively cleaved form, human cathelicidin, primates, mammals, animals; UCLL1)
02750.Additional_info:
Sequence analysis:APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows 65.5% similarity to ALL-38. It is an alternative processed form of hCAP-18, the precursor of human LL-37 and ALL-38.

Activity: Active against S. aureus, S. epidermidis, and Group A Streptococcus.

Immune modulation: TLN-58 upregulated IL-17C, IL-8, IL-23, IL-1alpha, and IL-1beta mRNA and protein expression in normal human keratinocytes, similar to LL-37. Updated 6/2024

02752.Name_Class: CrustinPm1 (antimicrobial protein; UCSS1a; ?S=S; modular design; natural AMPs; shrimp; Crustaceans, arthropods, invertebrates, animals; BBL)
02752.Additional_info: Sequence analysis:APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows 19.7% similarity to MrCrs. Active primarily against Gram-positive S. aureus (MIC 2.5-10 uM), M. luteus (MIC 20-50 uM), and Gram-negative bacteria, E. coli 363 (MIC 50-80 uM). The peptide is helical based on CD studies (Arayamethakorn S et al., 2016).

02751.Name_Class: HEdefensin (UCSS1a; 3S=S, natural AMPs; hard ticks, arachnids, Chelicerata, arthropods, invertebrates, animals; alternative form tested: HlDFS2)
02751.Additional_info:
Nomenclature: The prefix HE denotes hemolymph, the tissue of origin of the EST database.

Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows 90.4% similarity to D. silvarum defensin.

Activity: A synthetic peptide showed virucidal activity against Langat virus (LGTV).

AMP significance:Relationship with disease: Till 2016, B. burgdorferi is the only bacterium recognized to be responsible for lyme disease which was transmitted to human via the bite of infected tick. Updated 10/2017; 7/2021.

02753.Name_Class: CrustinPm7 (antimicrobial protein; UCSS1a; ?S=S; modular design; natural AMPs; shrimp; Crustaceans, arthropods, invertebrates, animals; BBL)

Sequence analysis:APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows 19.7% similarity to MrCrs.

Activity:Active against Gram-positive S. aureus, M. luteus, and Gram-negative bacteria, E. coli 363 (MIC 2-10 uM). The peptide is helical based on CD studies (Arayamethakorn S et al., 2016).

02754.Name_Class: DefMT2 (defensin MT2; UCSS1a; 3S=S, natural AMPs; hard ticks, arachnids, Chelicerata, arthropods, invertebrates, animals)

02755.Name_Class: DefMT7 (defensin MT7; UCSS1a; 3S=S, natural AMPs; hard ticks, arachnids, Chelicerata, arthropods, invertebrates, animals)
02755.Additional_info:

Activity: The peptide showed no activity against bacteria. This study found antimalarial activity, establishing it as an AMP.

02756.Additional_info: This Scorpions-Ticks Defensins Ancestor (STiDA) shows 69.8% similarity to Scapularisin-6. The entire sequences of the two STiDA peptides differ slightly.

02758.Name_Class: ToAP1 (ToAP-1, natural AMPs; scorpions, arachnids, Chelicerata, arthropods, invertebrates, animals; XXA; UCLL1c)

02759.Name_Class: ToAP2 (natural AMPs; scorpions, arachnids, Chelicerata, arthropods, invertebrates, animals; UCLL1a)

02760.Name_Class: ToAP3 (ToAP-3, Im4; Ile-rich; natural AMPs; scorpions, arachnids, Chelicerata, arthropods, invertebrates, animals; XXA; UCLL1c)
02760.Additional_info:

02763.Name_Class: Phylloseptin-PBa (natural AMPs; frog, amphibians, animals; UCLL1a)

02761.Name_Class: Con10 (natural AMPs; scorpions, arachnids, Chelicerata, arthropods, invertebrates, animals; UCLL1a)
02761.Additional_info:
Sequence analysis:APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows 64.3% similarity to scorpion VpAmp2.0.

Activity: Active against C. albicans SC5314 (MIC 100 uM), C. tropicalis ATCC 750 (MIC 12.5 uM), C. parapsilosis ATCC 22019 (MIC 200 uM), C. glabrata ATCC 90030 (MIC 200 uM), C. neoformans H99 serotype A (MIC 50 uM), and C. neoformans B3501 serotype D (MIC 25 uM). The Con10 scorpion peptide inhibited the biofilm formation of different A. baumannii in the concentration range of 12.5-25 uM. Upated 4/2019.

02762.Name_Class: NDBP-5.8 (natural AMPs; scorpions, arachnids, Chelicerata, arthropods, invertebrates, animals; UCLL1a)
02762.Additional_info:

02765.Name_Class: Thaulin-1 (Gly-rich; natural AMPs; frog, amphibians, animals; UCLL1a; No activity: Thaulin-2, Thaulin-4; weak activity: Thaulin-3)

02766.Name_Class: S. scrofa lysozyme (SSL; antimicrobial protein; natural AMPs; pigs, mammals; animals; UCSS1a; Derivatives: LP and SP)

02767.Name_Class: YD1 (natural AMPs; Gly-rich; bacteriocin, bacteria, prokaryotes; BBN)

Active against Gram- S. typhimurium KCTC 1925 (MIC 32 ug/ml), E. coli KCTC 1923 (MIC 8 ug/ml), P. aeruginosa KCTC 1637 (MIC 16 ug/ml), Gram+ M. smegmatis ATCC 9341 (MIC 8 ug/ml), S. aureus KCTC 1928, MRSA B15 (MIC 32 ug/ml), E. faecalis ATCC 29212 (MIC 64 ug/ml), B. subtilis ATCC 6633 (MIC 64 ug/ml), M. luteus ATCC 9341 (MIC 64 ug/ml), VRE 2, and VRE5 (MIC 64 ug/ml) (anti-VRE). YD1 binds to the plasmid DNA of E. coli (Rahman M et al., 2017).

Updated 2/2017; 10/2024.

02768.Name_Class: Bacteriocin TSU4 (natural AMPs; bacteria, prokaryotes; BWQ, unclassified)

02777.Additional_info:
The amino acid analysis (including D and L types) of the molecule was initially reported in 1978 (Kato T et al., 1978). A full sequence and activity characterization was achieved recently (see the ref). APD analysis reveals that the sequence of THE PEPTIDE shows 37.5% similarity to Paenibacterin .

Activity: Mainly active against G- bacteria (see beloe) and only weakly active against Gram+ B. subtilis JH642 (MIC 50 uM), S. aureus ATCC 25923 (MIC 100 uM), Gram- food pathogens C. jejuni NCTC 11168 (MIC 100 uM), E. coli DH5alpha (MIC 50 uM), and S. enterica serovar Typhimurium (MIC 25 uM). Also active against resistant strains of K. pneumoniae, A. baumannii, and E. coli. It is not active (MIC>100 uM) against C.maltaromaticum UAL26, E.faecium ATCC 19434, L.lactis subsp. cremoris HP, L.monocytogenes ATCC 15313, P.polymyxa NRRL B-30509, P.acidilactici PAC 1.0, and P.aeruginosa ATCC 15442. <

Chemical modification: Warning: the sequence is represented as a close mimic. In particular, there are two D-type 2,4-diaminobutyrate (Dab), represented by K's here. In addition, residue V1, S4, W5, and I12 are also D-amino acids.

MOA:bacteria: this peptide binds to lipid II of Gram-negative bacteria.

Structure: NMR studies in lipid II doped DPC micelles revealed specific interactions (Cochrane SA et al., 2016). You can rotate, zoom, and view the lipid II bound 3D structure here in the PDB.

SAR: A synthetic form with an Octanoyl chain retained the the activity against E. coli ATCC 25922 (MIC 3.1 uM), S. enterica ATCC 13311 (MIC 6.25 uM), P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853 (MIC 25 uM), C. jejuni NCTC 11168 (MIC 1.56), K. pneumoniae ATCC 13883 (MIC 3.13), A. baumannii ATCC 19606 (MIC 12.5 uM), E. faecalis ATCC29212 (MIC 100 uM), S. aureus ATCC 29213 (MIC 100 uM), L. monocytogenes ATCC 15313 (MIC 25 uM), and E. faecium ATCC 19434 (MIC 50 uM). Ala scan identified critical amino acids for activity. The antimicrobial activity of the analogues is directly correlated to their ability to adopt a stable secondary structure in a membrane environment (Cochrane SA et al., 2014). H-TriA1, a much less active form, does not contain an unacylated chain.

Updated 10/2017.

02816.Additional_info:
